newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Bullish Australian stocks bolt to record close.
newsitem.headline: Bullish Australian stocks bolt to record close.

text.p: A bullish Australian stock market bolted to a record close on Tuesday, capturing an intra-day high along the way as the local market played catch-up with soaring U.S. markets.

The All Ordinaries Index climbed 28 points to a close of 2,628.9, surpassing the previous record close of 2,625.7 reached on June 2. Earlier in the day the market hit an intra-day high of 2,631.3, topping the previous high of 2,626.0.
"The blue chips are just rocketing ahead," said dealer Justin Hondris of brokerage Hartley Poynton, who said rate-sensitive sectors were the most buoyant.

"It's mainly in the banks and the interest rate-sensitive stocks but anything with a yield is doing well. People are finally coming to the conclusion that this market is good value compared to having your money in fixed interest."
Banking shares were certainly winners on the day, the sector index leaping 2.1 percent compared to a 1.1 percent gain in the benchmark All Ordinaries index.
Frequently touted as likely targets for foreign predators, ANZ Banking Group jumped 2.7 percent to close at A$9.338 (US$7.10), while Westpac Banking Corp leapt four percent to A$7.46.
Foster's Brewing featured in turnover lists with 9.9 million shares traded, recovering some of Friday's losses to close up four cents at A$2.57.

Bellwether BHP added one percent to A$18.92 in the wake of last week's placement of its 36.5 percent Foster's stake and amid talk of a merger of the giant Gorgon and North West Shelf gas fields off Western Australia.
Rises outnumbered falls by a ratio of about nine to seven, while about 29 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
